Wald, profile, or parametric-bootstrap intervals for a conditional CJS fit

Source: R/cjs-methods.R
confint.drm_cjs.Rd

Wald, profile, or parametric-bootstrap intervals for a conditional CJS fit

Usage

# S3 method for class 'drm_cjs'
confint(
  object,
  parm,
  level = 0.95,
  method = c("wald", "profile", "bootstrap"),
  nsim = 200L,
  seed = NULL,
  min_usable = 100L,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A drm_cjs fit.

parm

Optional coefficient names or indices. For constant individual or shared SD profiles, use "sd:phi" or "sd:p". For an individual or shared SD formula, use a fitted coefficient name such as "sd_phi:z" or "sd_p:z".

level

Confidence level.

method

"wald", "profile", or "bootstrap".

nsim

Bootstrap attempts.

seed

Optional bootstrap seed.

min_usable

Minimum usable bootstrap fits before percentile intervals are returned.

...

Unused.

Value

An interval matrix with method diagnostics in attributes. The bootstrap attempts attribute retains convergence, quadrature, curvature, and numerical zero-SD diagnostics separately. Profile and parametric-bootstrap intervals are available for native integrated individual-effect fits. Wald intervals additionally require nonsingular interior curvature. Bootstrap eligibility is recorded separately from Wald curvature and requires finite converged estimates with accepted quadrature refinement for integrated fits. Bootstrap intervals require at least min_usable refits; availability does not establish calibration. Constant shared SD limits exponentiate finite interior log-SD profile endpoints and do not evaluate an exact-zero model. Shared-effect fixed-coefficient and SD-formula profile intervals require a stationary positive-curvature latent mode; shared-effect Wald and bootstrap intervals remain unavailable. Fixed-effect rows are on the coefficient scale. Ordinary individual coefficient profiles require refined fitted integration, rebuild and refine each constrained point over the saved quadrature ladder, and withhold limits when the refitted center disagrees with or improves on the fitted likelihood, any constrained point improves on the fitted likelihood, or an endpoint fails its numerical check. If any constrained point improves on the fit, both endpoint limits are withheld. Availability does not establish calibration. Individual sd:phi and sd:p profile rows are on the SD scale. Their exact-zero endpoint is evaluated with the selected effect removed and the remaining CJS model reoptimized. A constrained endpoint is withheld when its optimizer fails or quadrature does not refine. SD-formula coefficients can also be profiled by their sd_phi:<column> or sd_p:<column> names for individual or shared effects; shared profile points re-solve the latent mode. Those limits use the log-SD coefficient scale. Profile availability does not establish calibration.
